questions.q: Which of these is the correct order of the six O2C lifecycle stages?
options: Billing, Capture, Collection, Fulfillment, Validation, Reconciliation
Reconciliation, Validation, Capture, Collection, Billing, Fulfillment
Capture, Validation, Fulfillment, Billing, Collection, Reconciliation
Fulfillment, Capture, Billing, Validation, Collection, Reconciliation
questions.explain: The order runs capture, validation, fulfillment, billing, collection, then reconciliation.

questions.q: Who is typically responsible for the order validation stage (credit checks and approvals)?
options: Credit and collections analysts, sometimes with manager approval
Warehouse staff
The customer themselves
The General Ledger accountant
questions.explain: Credit and collections analysts, often alongside an Approval Management (AME) rule, own the validation stage.

questions.q: Which Oracle Fusion area is primarily responsible for the fulfillment stage?
options: General Ledger
Cash Management
Subledger Accounting
Inventory Management and Shipping
questions.explain: Fulfillment — picking, packing, and shipping — happens in Inventory Management and Shipping.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where do most real-world Order-to-Cash problems actually occur?
options: Inside a single screen, in isolation
At the handoffs between stages and between the people who own them
Only in the General Ledger
They are evenly distributed and unpredictable
questions.explain: Most problems happen at the handoff points — e.g., a shipment that doesn't match the order, or billing run too early.

questions.q: What is the most useful first question when troubleshooting a stuck O2C transaction?
options: Which database table stores this field?
What font does the invoice use?
Whose stage was this transaction in, and what does their screen show right now?
How many lines does the sales order have?
questions.explain: Identifying which role/stage owns the transaction right now is the fastest path to finding where it's stuck.
